set.approach: From the Twenty Mile Lakes trailhead north of McCall, follow the Twenty Mile Lakes trail and keep left at the fork, climbing through burnt forest and alpine meadow to the first lake. Pass the lake on its right to a ridge, follow the crest left through deadfall toward East Lake, and just short of it climb straight up the hillside to the low point joining Storm Peak and Storm Dome. Traverse toward Storm Dome to the second notch from the dome, marked by a large cairn, then drop down the steep gully and the slippery grassy ramp below it. Descend the talus (or angle right across grassy ledges to the foot of the wall) to the meadow by Storm Peak Lake, where parties camp below the face. The route starts on a clean, low-angle slab at the left side of the wall, below a high first bolt.
set.descent_text: The route can be rappelled with a single 70 m rope.

review.notes: Approach from the Storm Dome area page, start from the route Location; rappel descent from the AAJ note on both routes (one source).

set.descent_text: Rappel from the top of the last pitch, or scramble left along an exposed ramp to the summit, staying roped.

review.notes: Descent from the route page (one source); approach as above.

set.approach: Both the north and east faces are reached from Merriam Lake. Park at the end of the Forest Service road that serves the lake and follow the good trail to the lake, where there are fine camp spots. The east face is the steep wall rising directly above the lake. The route begins to the left of East Face Direct, next to the dihedral chimney that cuts the center of the wall.
set.descent_text: From the east-face summit, head north and descend the scree fields, keeping the north ridge to your right and the main summit above you on the left. Walk down and east to a small creek and follow the water back to Merriam Lake.

review.notes: Approach from area page and both route pages; descent from the route page only.

set.approach: Park at the Lion Creek water slides lot, pass through the concrete barricades and follow cairns and rough paths down to the creek crossing. Then work up and to the left over boulders and scree, passing a few cairns, until you stand under the slabs. The route is reached by climbing the lower pitches of The Lion King to a big evergreen with an anchor, then traversing left and downclimbing into a big gully. Follow the gully up to a boulder blocking it, look left for a short class 4 scramble, and climb it to a bolted anchor that begins the route.
set.descent_text: The bolted anchor at the start of the route doubles as the way back down to the gully. At the top of the corner, an anchor up and to the right can be used to rappel.

review.notes: Route page gives the link-up from The Lion King; South Dome and Lion Creek pages give the walk to the slabs.

set.approach: Start at the Harrison Lake parking area, where Beehive Dome is in view. The approach is mostly bushwhacking, with a marshy creek crossing and a short scramble to the base of the dome. Go around the dome to the far left, where the slab eases to third class, and walk up it to the first summit.
set.descent_text: The route ends on the last of the traverse's summits. Return along the ridge the way you came, then turn off and drop to Harrison Lake over a small ridge. Cross the rocks by the lake and take the Harrison Lake trail back to the trailhead.

review.notes: Both pages agree on the Harrison Lake start, the left side of the dome and the exit by the lake and trail.

set.descent_text: The standard way off goes down the north side of the ridge and around the north side of the gendarme to regain the ridge west of it, with several exposed class 5 slab moves and traverses.

review.notes: Descent only, one source; approach to the start is not described from a trailhead, so omitted.

set.approach: Start from the Leatherman Peak trailhead and head due west, keeping north of the ridge between Borah and Merriam Lake. Follow a small creek to a small lake under a cliff and pass the cliff on its south side. Cross the scree to a series of limestone bands running north and follow them to the top of the East Direct line, below the summit block.
set.descent_text: There is no easy way down the line of ascent. Descend Chicken Out Ridge to the saddle, then drop the steep eastern slope, which holds snow early and loose scree later.

review.notes: Single route page; both texts are its own account.
